# Cryptic Teacher

**[cryptic.paultarjan.com](https://cryptic.paultarjan.com)**

A static web app, with no framework and no backend, that teaches you to solve
cryptic crosswords. It uses real published puzzles and gives each clue an
escalating **hint ladder** instead of a bare answer key. The rungs, in ladder
order:

<!-- LADDER-START generated by tools/build_readme.py — do not edit -->
1. **Spot the indicator words** — the anagram, container, reversal and homophone signal words are highlighted.
2. **Where is the definition?** — the definition part of the clue is highlighted.
3. **What kind of clue is this?** — anagram? charade? container? hidden word? …
4. **The building blocks** — the fodder and the synonym breakdown, a piece at a time (“host = ARMY; part of TV duo = ANT”). A double definition has none: its halves are the definition rung's.
5. **Full walkthrough** — the whole assembly, step by step.

**Fill in answer** writes the solution into the grid. It is the way out of a clue rather than a step in it, so it is offered alongside the rungs once the building blocks are up, and it is not counted as one.
<!-- LADDER-END -->

How the ladder behaves:

- **A rung asks before it tells.** Every rung except the walkthrough asks its
  question first. The indicator, definition and building-blocks rungs ask
  "which words?", and you answer by tapping words in the clue. The type rung
  offers the seven clue families to pick from. Answer correctly and you get the
  rung without spending a hint. "Just tell me" reveals it at the normal cost. A
  rung you worked out is scored separately from one you bought.
- **A piece with only one possible answer is handed over, not asked.** If the
  other rungs have already claimed every other word of the clue, tapping the
  rest would be a question with one answer.
- **The ladder is tiers, not a chain.** The three spotting rungs (indicators,
  definition, type) can be taken in any order. The building blocks and the
  walkthrough stay locked until the spotting rungs are up.
- **Solving the clue unlocks every rung for free.**

Other features:

- **Reveal one letter** is available at any time. It does not advance the
  ladder, but it counts against your score.
- **Report a bad hint** is on every clue: two taps and a sentence, with the
  puzzle and clue filled in for you.
- **Check** buttons (letter / entry / grid) mark wrong letters without
  revealing answers.
- A gentle score: clues solved with no hints, rungs shown, rungs worked out.
- A collapsible "How cryptic clues work" tutorial.
- A **glossary of standard abbreviations**. The building-blocks rung links into
  it word by word.
- A puzzle picker.
- Progress is saved in localStorage, per puzzle.

<!-- CORPUS-START generated by tools/build_readme.py — do not edit -->
**Corpus** — 22,735 puzzles across 13 series (Guardian cryptic 8414, Independent daily 3534, Times cryptic 3071, Times Quick Cryptic 2521, Guardian Quiptic 1400, Observer Everyman 1202, Independent Sunday 586, Sunday Times cryptic 564, Private Eye Cyclops 519, Times Jumbo 512, Globe and Mail cryptic 269, scanned book reprints 84, Metro cryptic 59). 947 of them are annotated clue-for-clue, all six rungs, machine-validated: 29,504 of 669,631 clues, or 4%. The rest are backlog the daily job is still draining — they show an <em>answers only</em> badge and degrade gracefully (checking and letter reveals still work; the teaching ladder appears once a puzzle is annotated).
<!-- CORPUS-END -->

## Run it

There is one build step. The puzzle list the app opens with, and the script
form of each puzzle, are generated from the committed puzzle files and are not
committed. After a fresh clone, build them once. It takes about ten seconds:

```
python3 tools/fetch_puzzle.py --reindex
```

This writes `puzzles/index.json`, `puzzles/index.js`, and one
`puzzles/<series>-<n>.js` per puzzle. It also restamps the `?v=` hashes in
`index.html`, so `git status` will show `index.html` as modified. Do not commit
that change. `python3 tools/stamp_assets.py --unstamp` puts the file back (see
"Cache busting" in `APP.md`).

Then do one of these:

- Open `index.html` directly in a browser. It works from `file://`.
- Run `python3 -m http.server 8017` in the repo root and visit
  <http://localhost:8017/>.
- Host on GitHub Pages. `.github/workflows/pages.yml` runs the same reindex
  command on its own checkout before it builds, so there is nothing to commit.
  All paths are relative and `.nojekyll` is included.

Re-run the reindex after fetching or annotating anything, if you want to see it
in the browser. The tools rebuild the index themselves before reading it:
`tools/smoke_test.js`, `tools/test_push_hold.js`, `tools/puzzle_integrity.py`
and `tools/build_readme.py` all do.

## Puzzle file format

`puzzles/<series>-<n>.json` holds one puzzle as plain JSON. It is the committed
source that every tool reads and writes. Next to it, generated and not
committed, `puzzles/<series>-<n>.js` assigns the same JSON to
`window.CRYPTIC_PUZZLES["<series>-<n>"]`, between `/*JSON-START*/` and
`/*JSON-END*/` markers. That script is how the page loads a puzzle from
`file://`.

Shape:

```jsonc
{
  "id": "cryptic-30066", "number": 30066, "name": "Cryptic crossword No 30,066",
  "setter": "Tramp", "date": 1784764800000, "dimensions": {"rows": 15, "cols": 15},
  "sourceUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/crosswords/cryptic/30066",
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": "16-across", "number": 16, "direction": "across",
      "position": {"x": 0, "y": 8}, "length": 10,
      "clue": "Destroying climate, sun reaches highest point (10)",
      "separatorLocations": {",": [7]},
      "solution": "CULMINATES",
      "annotation": {
        "type": "anagram",
        "answer": "CULMINATES",
        "definition": "reaches highest point",
        "indicators": ["Destroying"],
        "anagram": {"fodder": "CLIMATE SUN"},
        "blocks": [{"clueFragment": "climate, sun", "gives": "CLIMATESUN", "note": "anagram fodder"}],
        "walkthrough": "…2-4 friendly sentences…"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Annotation rules

`tools/validate_annotations.py` enforces these:

- `definition`, `definition2` and each `indicators[]` string must appear
  **verbatim** in the clue text. Guardian clues use `’` and `–`.
- The letters of `answer` must equal the grid solution. For linked clues, that
  is the whole group.
- Letter mechanics must be machine-checkable:
  - `anagram.fodder` must be a multiset match for the answer.
  - `pieces` must concatenate to the answer.
  - `subAnagrams` and `subReversals` verify embedded steps.
  - A hidden answer must appear inside the clue's letters.
- Linked entries: the group's first entry carries the full annotation and
  `"coversGroup": true`. The others carry `{"linkedTo": "<first-id>"}`.
- **An absent key means empty.** An un-annotated entry has no `annotation` key
  at all. The app then badges the puzzle `answers only` and shows no ladder.
  `separatorLocations` works the same way: it is present only when the paper
  marks a break inside the answer. Nothing writes `{}` or `null` into a puzzle
  file.

### Provenance: where the puzzle, its grid and its answers each came from

Every puzzle has a `provenance` block next to `sourceUrl`. `sourceUrl` is only a
link to the page the puzzle was printed on. `provenance` records how the file
got here and, most importantly, **whose answers these are**.

```jsonc
"sourceUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/crosswords/everyman/3716",
"provenance": {
  "publisher": "Observer",          // from tools/series.py, by the id's series
  "series": "everyman",             // read off the id, never the `series` field
  "acquiredBy": "tools/fetch_wayback.py",   // the command that actually ran
  "acquiredOn": "2026-09-17",       // when the file first appeared in git
  "retrievedFrom": "wayback",       // publisher | wayback | blog | book | authored
  "retrievedUrl": "https://web.archive.org/web/2016id_/https://…",
  "gridOrigin": "published",        // published | reconstructed | authored
  "solutionOrigin": "published",    // published | writeup | model | authored | unsolved
  "annotatedBy": ["claude-opus-5"]  // who wrote the hints: exact model ids, or human | published | unknown
}
```

**The clues, the grid and the answers can each come from a different place.**
That is why these are separate fields. Two examples:

- A Cyclops puzzle comes from Private Eye's own `.puz` download. Private Eye
  blanks the solution grid, so the answers come from a fifteensquared write-up:
  `retrievedFrom: publisher`, `solutionOrigin: writeup`.
- A scanned-book puzzle has three origins. The clues come from a book scan, the
  grid is reconstructed here from those clues, and the answers are solved here
  by a model.

**Read `solutionOrigin` before trusting a grid:**

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `published` | The setter's own answer key. Ground truth. |
| `writeup` | A human solver's published answers, not the setter's. |
| `model` | We solved it from the clues. Self-consistent and crossing-checked, but still a guess. |
| `authored` | We wrote the puzzle. |
| `unsolved` | The grid is empty. This is a known fact, not missing data. |

A grid we guessed must never look the same as one the paper answered. This
field keeps them apart.

Other fields:

- `previousSolutionOrigin` appears when the answers in the file replaced answers
  of a different origin. Example: a grid was cold-solved, then the paper
  published the same answers.
- `annotatedBy` is on every puzzle with hints and says who wrote them: exact
  model ids such as `claude-opus-5`, never an alias like `opus`, because an alias
  points at a different model from one month to the next. One entry per run, in
  the order they ran; a run that was cut off and resumed by the same model
  counts once. `tools/apply_annotations.py` writes it from the running
  session's transcript. Hints no model wrote say `human` or `published`.
- `solutionSource`, where present, is the detail behind `solutionOrigin`: which
  write-up, which model, whether an official key can ever exist. The validator
  rejects a file where the two disagree.
- The canonical URL is **not** copied into the block. It lives only in
  `sourceUrl`, because a second copy is a second thing that can be wrong.
- `retrievedUrl` is null for the 542 puzzles recovered from archive captures
  before the field existed. The capture address was never stored, and guessing
  it would be worse than admitting it is unknown.

Every allowed value is listed in `tools/provenance.py` and nowhere else.
`tools/puzzle_integrity.py` validates against those same dicts.
`tools/test_provenance.sh` proves it: it deletes a value and checks that the
corpus is then rejected. `tools/backfill_provenance.py` writes the block. It is
idempotent and safe to re-run. New puzzles get the block automatically, because
`write_puzzle_file` stamps it on every write.

## Adding puzzles

For the Guardian series:

```
python3 tools/fetch_puzzle.py 30123           # one puzzle
python3 tools/fetch_puzzle.py --latest        # newest cryptic (no-op if already present)
python3 tools/fetch_puzzle.py --backfill 30   # the last 30, skipping ones you have
```

Other papers have their own `tools/fetch_*.py` scripts, listed in
`docs/LAYOUT.md`.

Then annotate the new `puzzles/<series>-<n>.json`, by hand or with Claude Code
using `tools/annotate_prompt.md`, and check it:

```
python3 tools/validate_annotations.py 30123
python3 tools/fetch_puzzle.py --reindex
```

### Checking your work

```
python3 tools/build_seo_pages.py        # the crawlable pages (generated, not committed)
node tools/smoke_test.js                # the app, driven headless against the whole corpus
python3 tools/validate_annotations.py   # no argument: every puzzle
python3 tools/build_readme.py --check   # this file still describes this repo
```

The smoke test reads `/learn/` and `/abbreviations/` the way a visitor gets
them, so build those pages first (about half a minute). The smoke test tells
you if they are missing.

If you edit `style.css`, `app.js` or a puzzle file, rebuild and restamp the
static pages. Otherwise the suite fails on hundreds of stale `?v=` references:

```
python3 tools/build_seo_pages.py && python3 tools/stamp_assets.py
bash tools/make_og.sh --all         # only redraws cards older than their puzzle
```

`tools/smoke_test.js` is the most important check. It runs the real `app.js`
against a fake DOM and the real puzzle files, so bad data fails it as readily
as bad code. For example: a rung that gives the answer away early, a
highlight that does not sit where the annotation says, or a sound clue that
never prints what it sounds like. **Assertions match the markup the app
emits, never an English phrase.** Annotation prose is written by a model and
will eventually contain any sentence you might use as a signal.

### Generated regions of this file

`tools/build_readme.py` generates three regions of this README: the hint
ladder, the corpus paragraph, and the scheduling defaults. It also generates
all of `docs/LAYOUT.md`. Each region sits between `<!-- NAME-START -->` and
`<!-- NAME-END -->` markers. The sources are the puzzle files, `app.js`,
`git ls-files` and the shell scripts.

- **Do not hand-edit inside the markers.**
- `python3 tools/build_readme.py` rewrites the regions.
  `python3 tools/build_readme.py --check` exits 1 if they are out of date.
- The check fails instead of leaving a wrong sentence. That happens when a tool
  has no description line, a described tool has been deleted, a new series has
  no display name, or a quoted default has been renamed. A rung renamed in
  `app.js` renames itself here.
- Each region has one builder function in `tools/build_readme.py`:
  `build_corpus()` counts the puzzle files for the corpus paragraph,
  `build_ladder()` reads `LABELS` in `app.js` for the rung list, and
  `build_knobs()` parses the defaults out of the shell scripts (`KNOB_FILES`).
  `build_layout()` writes `docs/LAYOUT.md` from the `LAYOUT` table.
- To put a number in the prose, add it to the builder in
  `tools/build_readme.py`, not here. A number typed by hand is never checked
  again.

## Nightly jobs

`tools/daily_update.sh` runs once a day on a machine with the `claude` CLI. In
order, it:

1. fetches the newest puzzles;
2. re-fetches any puzzle still waiting for published solutions
   (`--refresh-unsolved`);
3. has Claude annotate the newest un-annotated puzzles, up to `ANNOTATE_MAX`
   per run;
4. validates, reindexes, commits, and pushes if a remote is configured.

It works newest first because that is where readers are: a puzzle gets most of
its visits in the week it comes out. Working oldest first would leave the top of
the site without hints forever. One puzzle a day would never catch up, because
the tracked series publish about fifteen puzzles a week between them.

<!-- KNOBS-START generated by tools/build_readme.py — do not edit -->
The two scheduled jobs split the quota deliberately: the 06:15 one annotates every puzzle from the last two days plus at most 3 from the backlog, and only below 90% of the week (and 70% of the rolling five-hour window, re-checked between puzzles), while the hourly one does nothing at all until `weekly_usage.py --resets-in` says the weekly window is within 1 hour of turning over — at which point unspent quota is about to vanish, so it spends the remainder with no gate.
<!-- KNOBS-END -->

The hourly job is `tools/prereset_backfill.sh`.

### Waiting for solutions: cold solving

The Guardian withholds solutions to its Saturday *Prize* crossword for about a
week. `--refresh-unsolved` re-checks every night until they appear.

So that the newest puzzle is not left without hints for that week, the daily
run also *solves* up to `SOLVE_MAX` puzzles a night from the clues alone:

- `tools/solve_packet.py` gives the model the clues and the grid's crossing map.
- `tools/solve_prompt.md` gives it the method.
- `tools/apply_solution.py` is the only way the answers reach the puzzle file.
  It writes nothing unless every entry is answered, every answer has the length
  the grid needs, and all crossing letters agree (about 58 on a typical grid).
- The answers are marked `solutionSource` in the file and `solutionsUnofficial`
  in the index. The site says so wherever it shows them.
- The puzzle keeps being re-fetched. When the official key lands, it replaces
  the model's answers and prints a `BLIND SOLVE GRADED n/30` line. The
  annotation of any clue the model got wrong is thrown away, so the queue
  rewrites it.

### Scheduling

Nothing in this repo schedules itself. There is no LaunchAgent, systemd unit or
crontab here. **There must be exactly one schedule.** A second scheduler is not
a fallback: both copies would annotate the same backlog out of the same weekly
quota.

The whole schedule is two lines:

```
15 6 * * * flock -n /tmp/cryptic-daily.lock /path/to/cryptic-teacher/tools/daily_update.sh >> /path/to/cryptic-teacher/.update.log 2>&1
5 * * * *  flock -n /tmp/cryptic-prereset.lock /path/to/cryptic-teacher/tools/prereset_backfill.sh >> /path/to/cryptic-teacher/.prereset.log 2>&1
```

- Output (stdout and stderr) goes to `.update.log` and `.prereset.log`. Both are
  untracked on purpose.
- `flock -n` is required on the second line. cron does not know whether the
  last run is still going, and two overlapping backfills would spend the same
  quota window.

### The `claude` credential

A scheduled run needs the `claude` CLI already logged in, as the user the
scheduler runs as.

- This works wherever the credential is a readable file:
  `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, or a directory named by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- It does not work where the credential is in a desktop keyring that only a GUI
  login session can unlock. **On macOS**, the CLI keeps its OAuth token in the
  login keychain. cron runs outside that session, so every run fails with
  `Not logged in · Please run /login` and the backlog never drains. On macOS,
  schedule the jobs with a per-user LaunchAgent in `gui/<uid>` instead of cron.
  Delete the crontab lines when you add it; do not run both.
- A scheduler gives a job a bare `PATH` that does not include
  `~/.local/bin/claude`. The scripts set an explicit `PATH` for that reason.
